newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer but recovery seen limited.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer but recovery seen limited.

text.p: COMEX copper settled firmer on Thursday as the market bounced back to recover some ground after the heavy selloff of the past week.
But any recovery in prices is largely complete with only a further cent or so of ground that could be regained, said Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities.
Copper prices had fallen more than 10 cents in the past week before the recovery began.
"We are in a slow demand period, and we may see some stabilization rather than bouncing up. Narrow ranges are what I would anticipate," she added.

LME stocks rose 1,625 tonnes Thursday to 124,750 tonnes, but traders cautioned that some of the hike was also due to arbitrage related dealings as July LME closed at a 2.40 cent premium over its COMEX counterpart.

September COMEX copper ended 2.10 cents firmer at 110.90 cents a lb, traded 111.10 to 109.70 cents. July settled 2.75 cents firmer at 111.95 cents. Spot June, which expired Thursday, went out 3.25 cents higher at 112.95 cents.
Volume was good at an estimated 17,000 lots.
The market is also keenly watching labor talks at Canada's Inco Ltd whose Sudbury mining operations have been on strike since June 2.
Inco produces some 90,000 tonnes a year of copper and supplies metal to the Northeastern region of the U.S.
Open interest in COMEX copper futures has tumbled from a recent peak of 61,295 lots on May 20 to 49,941 lots by close Wednesday.
Although there is continued, heavy liquidation in July by the funds, dealers said, they were not putting on fresh positions in most-active September whose open interest rose just 222 lots Wednesday.
